title: Astro Portal session event payload: mount_goto
description: A GoTo the person asked of the mount, with how it went. One event per outcome, so a GoTo that never arrived stays visible: `sent` — the mount accepted the slew; `arrived` — the mount stopped slewing within one degree of the target (`gapDegrees` is the gap read from the mount); `refused` — nothing moved (`refusedBy` says who). A reader that shows one line per GoTo keeps `arrived` and `refused` and shows `sent` only when neither follows for the same target. Recorded by the application from the driver's own code path with the night's clock; every field but the ones marked required is optional, and a reader tolerates a payload without them. Private in a shared night. See session-events.md.

targetId.description: The plan's key of the target the mount was sent to, the same one the target events use (a calibration star or a polar-alignment move carries its own key).

targetLabel.description: The target's display name (« M110 »), for a reader that cannot resolve `targetId`.

gapDegrees.description: Optional: the angular gap, in degrees, between where the device said it pointed and the target, read from the device when it reports a position. Absent means the device said nothing of where it pointed.

refusedBy.description: Optional, with `outcome: refused`: who refused — `safety` the application's own pointing safety (horizon mask, zenith, cables, Sun) before any byte was sent; `mount` the mount itself; `no_coordinates` the target has no fixed position to point at.

reason.description: Optional, with `outcome: refused`: a short machine code of the cause (`below_horizon`, `parked`, `not_aligned`, `zenith`…), never a sentence.

protocol.description: Optional: the mount's protocol as the application names it (`LX200`, `Alpaca`, `INDI`, `SynScan`, `iOptron`, `NexStar`).
